section.title: Overview
section.para: This module contains REGISTER processing logic for the S-CSCF. The 'storage engine' of this module is provided by the ims_usrloc_scscf module:

section.title: &kamailio; Modules
section.para:
The following modules must be loaded before this module:
CDP
CDP_AVP
TM
ims_usrloc_scscf

section.title: External Libraries or Applications
section.para:
The following libraries or applications must be installed before running &kamailio; with this module loaded:
LibXML2 - used for parsing the XML Subscription information obtained from the HSS (Home Subscriber Server)

section.title: default_expires (int)
section.para: If the processed message contains neither Expires HFs nor expires contact parameters, this value will be used for newly created S-CSCF usrloc records. The parameter contains number of second to expire (for example use 3600 for one hour). If it is set to a lower value than the min_expires parameter then it will be ignored. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework. A random value in a specific interval can be selected by using the default_expires_range parameter

section.title: default_expires_range (int)
section.para: This parameter specifies that the expiry used for newly created S-CSCF usrloc records are not fixed(when default_expires applies), but a random value in the intervalrdq [default_expires-default_expires_range%, default_expires+default_expires_range%]. The value is between 0 and 100 and represent the maximum percentage from default_expires that will be subtracted or added when computing the value. Default in 0, meaning default_expires is left unmodified. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

section.title: min_expires (int)
section.para: The minimum expires value of a Contact, values lower than this minimum will be automatically set to the minimum. Value 0 disables the checking. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

section.title: max_expires (int)
section.para: The maximum expires value of a Contact, values higher than this maximum will be automatically set to the maximum. Value 0 disables the checking. This parameter can be modified via ser config framework.

section.title: subscription_default_expires (int)
section.para: If the processed message contains neither Expires HFs nor expires contact parameters, this value will be used for newly created subscriptions. The parameter contains number of second to expire (for example use 3600 for one hour). If it is set to a lower value than the subscription_min_expires parameter then it will be ignored. A random value in a specific interval can be selected by using the subscription_expires_range parameter

section.title: subscription_expires_range (int)
section.para: This parameter specifies that the expiry used for newly created subscriptions are not fixed(when subscription_default_expires applies), but a random value in the interval [subscription_default_expires-subscription_expires_range%, subscription_default_expires+subscription_expires_range%]. The value is between 0 and 100 and represent the maximum percentage from subscription_default_expires that will be subtracted or added when computing the value. Default in 0, meaning subscription_default_expires is left unmodified.

section.title: subscription_min_expires (int)
section.para: The minimum expires value of a subscription, values lower than this minimum will be automatically set to the minimum. Value 0 disables the checking.

section.title: subscription_max_expires (int)
section.para: The maximum expires value of a subscription, values higher than this maximum will be automatically set to the maximum. Value 0 disables the checking.

section.title: ue_unsubscribe_on_dereg (int)
section.para: Many UEs do not unsubscribe on de-register, therefor if the parameter is set to 0, the default, any subscription of that subscriber will be removed and NOTIFY will be not sent. To disable this behaviour set this parameter to 1.

section.title: cxdx_forced_peer (string)
section.para: FQDN of Diameter Peer (HSS) to use for communication (SAR). If you use this, the routing defined in your diameter xml configuration file (CDP) will be ignored and as a result you will lose the benefits of load balancing and failover.

section.title: append_branches (integer)
section.para: The parameter controls how lookup function processes multiple contacts. If there are multiple contacts for the given username in usrloc and this parameter is set to 1, Request-URI will be overwritten with the highest-q rated contact and the rest will be appended to sip_msg structure and can be later used by tm for forking. If the parameter is set to 0, only Request-URI will be overwritten with the highest-q rated contact and the rest will be left unprocessed. This parameter can be modified via Kamailio config framework.

section.title: method_filtering (integer)
section.para: Tells if the contact filtering based on supported methods should be performed during lookup. It's enabled only if it has a non zero value.

section.title: user_data_always (integer)
section.para: If specified this will make the S-CSCF always request user data from HSS.

section.title: error_reply_code (int)
section.para: In certain error conditions, the S-CSCF may not be able to process the request (e.g. in case of database failures). Per default and according to the Specs, the S-CSCF would return a 500 error in this case. However, according to the SIP-Specs for DNS-SRV, this won't trigger a failover, which may be desired.
This parameter let's you override the default 500 with another return-code (e.g. 503) in order to get the desired behaviour.

section.title: skip_multiple_bindings_on_reg_resp (int)
section.para: If set to 1 - on Re-Registration registrar sends in 200 OK reply only current contact in case of multiple bindings. If set to 0 - on Re-Registration registrar sends in 200 OK reply all contacts in case of multiple bindings according to RFC3261.

section.title: scscf_restoration_info_enabled (int)
section.para: If set to 1, the S-CSCF takes part in the S-CSCF restoration procedures of 3GPP TS 23.380 using the HSS rather than a database: every Cx Server-Assignment-Request carries a Supported-Features AVP naming IMSRestorationInd (3GPP TS 29.229 table 7.1.1), and those sent for a REGISTRATION or RE_REGISTRATION also back up the contact at the HSS in an SCSCF-Restoration-Info AVP: the whole Contact header field value, its Path and the Call-ID of the REGISTER. The HSS hands them back in the answer to a NO_ASSIGNMENT or UNREGISTERED_USER request sent by assign_server() for a user it holds as registered, and the S-CSCF then binds that contact again and serves the user as registered.

Only the contact of the first Contact header is backed up, and only when the REGISTER has a Path (see use_path). The restored binding is granted the registration time of the REGISTER it was backed up from, counted from the moment it is restored.

Enable it only towards an HSS that supports IMSRestorationInd. The Supported-Features AVP goes out with the M bit set on a request that carries SCSCF-Restoration-Info (3GPP TS 29.229 7.2.1), so an HSS without the feature rejects every REGISTRATION and RE_REGISTRATION request, and with it the REGISTER.

The function processes a REGISTER message. It can add, remove or modify usrloc records depending on Contact and Expires HFs in the REGISTER message. On success and when called from the REQUEST_ROUTE, 200 OK will be returned listing all contacts that are currently in usrloc. On an error, error message will be sent with a short description in reason phrase. In case of internal errors the function will return FALSE, otherwise a force to exit the cfg is file is actioned by returning 0 (asynchronous processing)
Meaning of the parameters is as follows:

listitem.para: async_reply_route- the route to execute after the save has completed. This is required because the save function is executed asynchronously (Diameter).
domain- Logical domain within registrar.
mode- Optional and unused legacy parameter.
flags- Optional parameter. Valid values: 0x01 - Realm is not used when extracting Private Identity from the Authorization header.

section.para: This function can be used from REQUEST_ROUTE, ONREPLY_ROUTE

This function extract the IMPU from the Request-URI and tries to find all registered contacts in usrloc. If there are no such contacts, -1 is returned. If there are, Request-URI will be rewritten with the contact that has the highest q value. The rest of the contacts will be appended to the sip msg structure (if append_branches is set) and can be later used by TM module for forking for example...
If the method filtering option is enabled, the lookup function will only return contacts that support the method of the request being processed (see allows header)
Meaning of the parameters is as follows:

listitem.para: domain - Logical domain within registrar.

section.para: Return codes:

listitem.para: -1 - Not found
-2 - Found, but method not allowed (check Allows header for INVITE, MESSAGE, etc).
-3 - Error occurred internally during processing

used in REQUEST_ROUTE

Sends a Cx Server-Assignment-Request on behalf of a request other than REGISTER, downloading the served user's profile into usrloc. The transaction is suspended and resumed in async_reply_route once the SAA arrives, with $avp(saa_return_code) set to 1 when a profile was stored and to a negative value otherwise. No reply is sent by the module; that is left to the route.
Meaning of the parameters is as follows:

listitem.para: async_reply_route - route to resume in when the SAA arrives.
domain - Logical domain within registrar.
direction - "orig" takes the served user from the P-Asserted-Identity, "term" from the Request-URI.
assignment_type - the Server-Assignment-Type, an integer or a variable holding one:

0 (NO_ASSIGNMENT) - fetch the profile without changing anything at the HSS. The HSS answers DIAMETER_UNABLE_TO_COMPLY when another S-CSCF is assigned to the user. An IMPU already in usrloc keeps its registration state and bindings; a new one is stored as unregistered. This is the S-CSCF restoration procedure for an originating request (3GPP TS 23.380 4.4.2).
3 (UNREGISTERED_USER) - fetch the unregistered profile and tell the HSS the user is unregistered here (3GPP TS 29.228 6.1.2.1).

With scscf_restoration_info_enabled, either answer can carry the restoration information backed up at REGISTER, for a user the HSS holds as registered. Each IMPU of the profile is then stored as registered with that contact bound to it; a contact still bound in usrloc is linked to the IMPU as it is.
Any other type is refused: REGISTRATION and RE_REGISTRATION are sent by save(), and the de-registration types would leave usrloc out of step with the HSS.

section.para: The function fetches the contacts for 'uri' from table 'domain' to pseudo-variable $ulc(profile) [ulc = ims scscf ulc].
